title: Shared definitions of the why documents

named_reasons.description: A reason for each named member. The names stay in the definition; only the reason is written here.

decisions.description: The design decisions with their reasons, so that a later change can tell what it overturns. Never name a repository or project; describe the requirement.

why.description: Why this decision and not the obvious alternative.

rejected.description: The alternative that was considered and why it was not taken. Omit it when none was.

out_of_scope.description: Plausible expectations that this deliberately does not cover, and who owns them.

owner.description: The workflow, action, task, rule or repository that is responsible instead.

limitations.description: What a successful run does not prove, so that success is not mistaken for more.

revisit_when.description: Situations in which the design should be questioned again, for example a case that would need one more input.

supported_variations.description: Legitimate requirements that the design supports on purpose, described as requirements and never by naming a repository or project. A variation without a reason does not belong here; a deviation that was not justified is removed instead.

requirement.description: The requirement that some repositories can have, stated generally.

why.description: Why it is a legitimate interest to deviate, and how the design supports it.

principles.description: The principles of the catalog that this design serves, each with how it does. Principles are predictability, stability, simplicity, consistency, frugality and reproducibility.

how.description: How the design serves the principle, or what it gives up for it.

description: Documents never name a repository or project, because that makes them age. They describe requirements, and say why a requirement is supported or why a variation was removed.
